answer_1.quote: Text style transfer (TST), an important task in natural language generation, aims to change the stylistic properties while preserving the style‑independent content within the context.
answer_1.outputs: Sentences generated with the target style (style‑transferred sentences)

answer_2.quote: We adopt transfer accuracy and content preservation to evaluate our method... The Bilingual Evaluation Understudy (BLEU) score can measure the similarity between two sentences at the lexical level... two BLEU scores are computed... self‑BLEU ... ref‑BLEU ... G‑score denotes the geometric mean of the self‑BLEU and S‑ACC.

answer_4.quote: We randomly select 200 outputs ... three annotators are asked to evaluate the generated sentence with a 6 score range from 1 (Very Bad) to 5 (Very Good) on style controlling (S), content preservation (C), and fluency (F).
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rated each generated sentence on three criteria—style controlling, content preservation, and fluency—using a 1‑5 Likert scale.
